mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over the prior 3 months signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS has declined by at least 0.1 percentage points over the prior 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) falls below 0.2%, it triggers an immediate monetary easing response that reduces equity discount rates, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS is at or below 0.2%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in employment (PAYEMS) and decrease in unemployment (UNRATE) over the prior month signals robust labor market conditions that accelerate consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises > 0.5% and UNRATE falls > 0.1pp in 1 month
failure_condition: The S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where PAYEMS rises > 0.5% and UNRATE falls > 0.1pp in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle economic expansion, a rising housing starts (HOUST) level signals continued consumer confidence and construction activity, which supports near-term equity returns; thus, positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns are expected when HOUST increases.
failure_condition: In the late-cycle expansion regime, the S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where HOUST rises > 0.5% in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over the prior 3 months signals improving labor market conditions that increase consumer spending and corporate profitability, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE has declined by at least 0.1 percentage points over the prior 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 550 thousand units, it indicates robust residential construction activity that correlates with strong consumer spending and economic expansion, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where HOUST exceeds 550.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in industrial production (INDPRO) and GDP (GDPC1) over the prior 3 months indicates robust economic expansion that increases corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO rises > 0.5% and GDPC1 rises > 0.1% over prior 3 months
failure_condition: The S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO rises > 0.5% and GDPC1 rises > 0.1% over the prior 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: In an inflationary pressure regime (CPIAUCSL > 215), rising consumer price inflation signals potential central bank tightening that increases equity discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL exceeds 215.
